delivery_banner: v0.5 deliverable · computed by KKME engine v7.3 · generated {{DATE}} · figures reproducible via the accompanying model
scope_lock: Scope as locked with the client 2026-07-22: independent revenue + EBITDA per project and consolidated, DA + intraday cashflows, FCR / aFRR / mFRR capacity + activation, dispatch physics at annual/monthly resolution, Central / Downside / Upside with Baltic saturation and cannibalisation, adjustable assumptions register, and the 8-line bridge from gross market revenues to pre-financing cash flow. Debt, interest and DSCR are excluded. Hourly chronological dispatch is v1.0 extended scope, agreed with the client.
override_mechanism: The `override` column is the adjustable handle. Enter a value there and it replaces the engine-derived `value` for that assumption; `value` is never overwritten, so the model's figure and your edit stay side by side. Overrides are applied by re-running the KKME engine — this workbook does not recompute the model. Excel formulas in it move only what is stated to be formula-linked (the scenario selector); every other figure is engine output.
scenario_selector_label: Selector over three pre-computed engine runs — not a live model. Each column below was produced by a full engine run under that scenario's six locked drivers; the dropdown chooses which of those runs is displayed.
excluded_items: Debt · interest · DSCR · tax — excluded from the commissioned bridge
_correlation_note: Deliberately absent. The correlation disclosure is computed by the portfolio runner and lives in portfolio.json as `correlation_note` — restating it here would create a second source for the same claim (discipline rule #4). Generators read it from the runner output.
reconciliation_note: Every figure in this deliverable is produced by the KKME engine and gated by an automated reconciliation harness: internal arithmetic identities (the bridge must tie out line by line, the portfolio must equal the sum of its projects) and external benchmark bands (published IRR ranges, CAPEX, cycle counts, margins). The harness runs on every regeneration and fails loudly. Its full result is reproduced in this deliverable.
figures_basis: All figures are computed by the KKME revenue engine v7.3 against the Baltic market state captured at generation time. Nothing in this deliverable is hand-entered: the workbook, the summary document and the engine are regenerated from the same run and are verified equal before delivery.
_glossary_provenance: Definitions follow docs/glossary.md, the codebase's canonical term list, so the deliverable cannot define a term differently from the engine that computes it.
glossary: aFRR
Automatic Frequency Restoration Reserve. Baltic balancing product, automatically activated. Paid a capacity price plus an activation energy price. The primary BESS revenue stream.
mFRR
Manual Frequency Restoration Reserve. Slower balancing product, manually activated. Lower activation frequency than aFRR. Also paid capacity plus activation.
FCR
Frequency Containment Reserve. The fastest response product. The Baltic FCR market is currently limited; this model carries FCR as a saturation diagnostic and takes no FCR revenue into the bridge.
S/D ratio
Supply/demand ratio for Baltic balancing capacity — flexible fleet MW against TSO procurement volume. Below 1.0× is scarcity (good for BESS); above 1.0× is price compression.
CPI
Competition Pressure Index. A KKME-derived measure of fleet growth against procurement demand, range 0.25–2.0. Not the consumer price index.
DA
Day-ahead market. Prices set one day before delivery by auction; the arbitrage revenue line is earned here.
COD
Commercial Operation Date. When the asset starts earning.
EFC
Equivalent full cycle. One complete charge and discharge of nameplate energy, however accumulated. The unit warranty throughput is stated in.
RTE
Round-trip efficiency. Energy out ÷ energy in, measured at the point of interconnection including auxiliaries.
BOL
Beginning of life. The as-commissioned state, before calendar and cycle degradation.
SoC
State of charge. Stored energy as a share of usable capacity.
BRP
Balance responsible party. The entity carrying imbalance risk for the asset; charged here as a flat annual fee.
POI
Point of interconnection. The grid connection point — all efficiency and capacity figures in this model are stated at the POI.
MOIC
Multiple on invested capital. Cumulative cash returned ÷ capital invested, undiscounted.
IRR
Internal rate of return. Project IRR (pre-leverage) is the primary metric here; the bridge's own NPV is pre-financing and pre-tax.
DSCR
Debt service coverage ratio. Out of scope for this engagement — no debt is modelled.
Pre-financing CF
Cash flow before any debt service, interest or tax. The last line of the commissioned bridge.
Optimiser fee
The route-to-market / trading-optimiser share of gross market revenues.
Augmentation
Mid-life addition of cells to restore usable energy lost to degradation.

revenue_lines._note: The client contract names ten revenue lines. At annual resolution the engine computes two revenue quantities — a combined balancing stream (rev_bal) and an energy-trading stream (rev_trd) — plus the charging cost rebuilt from the engine's own charged-MWh volumes. This table maps each contracted line onto the quantity that carries it and states the formula the engine actually evaluates, verbatim from the code. Where the engine does not resolve a contracted line separately, the row says so rather than presenting an invented split. Resolving all ten into their own settled cash lines requires the chronological hourly dispatch of v1.0 extended scope.

formulae.rev_bal: rev_bal = R_yr × bal_calibration × MW × min(1, bal_scale) × operating_year_fraction, where R_yr = R_cap_yr + R_act_yr summed over aFRR and mFRR: R_cap(product) = reservePrice(sd_ratio, product_share × capacity_price) × bidAcceptance(product_sd), R_act(product) = reservePrice(sd_ratio × 1.15, product_share × activation_rate × clearing_price × factor) × bidAcceptance(product_sd). bal_calibration anchors the curve to the observed Baltic balancing €/MW-yr; bal_scale is the energy-stacking constraint from usable MWh.
formulae.rev_trd: rev_trd = captured_spread_30d_mean × spread_mult(cal_year) × market_depth(sd_ratio) × RTE(yr) × trading_realisation × DA_MWh_per_MW_yr × trading_fraction × availability × degradation_ratio × MW × operating_year_fraction.
formulae.charging_costs: charging_costs = charged_MWh(yr) × mean observed charging price (€/MWh), where charged_MWh is the engine's own DA arbitrage throughput. The engine prices arbitrage on a captured spread already net of charging, so this line rebuilds the cost and gross less charging returns the engine gross exactly.
formulae.rev_gross: rev_gross = max(revenue_floor × MW × operating_year_fraction, rev_bal + rev_trd). The floor is a saturated-market minimum, not an expectation.

revenue_lines.split_caveat: The four aFRR/mFRR terms above are computed inside the balancing revenue and are not settled out as separate annual cash lines. Where this deliverable reports a capacity/activation split, it is the engine's reporting split of rev_bal at 65/35 — indicative, not separately computed. rev_bal is the computed quantity.
revenue_lines.fcr_caveat: No FCR revenue is claimed anywhere in this model. The Baltic FCR market is small relative to aFRR and mFRR procurement, and the engine treats FCR as a saturation diagnostic only. If FCR procurement deepens, that is upside not in these numbers.
